m: Salutation to Shri Ganesha. The seer said: That Goddess of tamas among the three qualities, and the one of sattva whom you have been told, is called Sharva, Chandika, Durga, Bhadra, and the blessed one.
The yoga-sleep of Hari is called Mahakali, of the quality of tamas, she whom the lotus-seated one praised for the destruction of Madhu and Kaitabha.
She has ten faces, ten arms, and ten feet, the lustre of collyrium, shining with a wide form and with a garland of thirty eyes.
Her teeth and fangs flash. Though her form is terrible, O lord of the earth, she is the foundation of the great splendours of form, good fortune, and beauty.
She bears sword, arrow, mace, spear, conch, discus, and sling, and she held an iron bar, a bow, and a head dripping blood.
She is that Vaishnavi illusion, Mahakali, hard to pass beyond. Worshipped, she would bring what moves and what does not move under the will of the one who performs the worship.
She who became manifest from the bodies of all the gods, of boundless splendour, of the three qualities, is Mahalakshmi, in person the crusher of the buffalo.
Her face is white, her arms are dark blue, the orbs of her breasts are very white, her waist is red, her feet are red, and her shanks and thighs are red and stately.
Her hips are beautifully varied. She is adorned with a many-coloured garland and garment, anointed with many colours, and rich in beauty, form, and good fortune.
She is to be worshipped as eighteen-armed, and she, the true one, is also thousand-armed. The weapons here will be told in order, beginning from the lower right hand.
A rosary, a lotus, an arrow, a sword, a thunderbolt, a mace, a discus, a trident, an axe, a conch, a bell, and a noose,
a spear, a staff, a shield, a bow, a drinking-cup, and a water-pot. With these weapons adorning her arms, she is seated on a lotus.
The one who worships this sovereign, consisting of all the gods, this Mahalakshmi, O king, becomes lord of all the worlds and of the gods.
She who arose from Gauri's body, resting in the single quality of sattva, is called Sarasvati in person, the destroyer of the asura Shumbha.
She held eight arms, arrows, a pestle, and she bears spear and discus, a conch, a bell, a plough, and a bow, O lord of the earth.
Worshipped with devotion, she gives the state of knowing all. She is the Goddess who crushes Nishumbha, the destroyer of the asura Shumbha.
These forms of the images have been told to you, O king. Hear the worship of the Mother of the world as it belongs to each of them separately.
When Mahalakshmi is to be worshipped, Mahakali and Sarasvati are to be worshipped on the right and the left, and the three pairs behind.
Virinchi with the woman of speech is in the middle, Rudra with Gauri on the right, and Hrishikesha with Lakshmi on the left. The triad of deities is in front.
One should worship the eighteen-armed one in the middle, the ten-faced one on her left, and the eight-armed great Lakshmi on the right.
When this eighteen-armed one is to be worshipped, O lord of men, then the ten-faced one and the eight-armed one are on the right and the left.
Kala and Mrityu are also to be worshipped fully, for the quieting of every calamity. And when the eight-armed one, destroyer of the asura Shumbha, is to be worshipped,
then her nine powers are to be worshipped, and Rudra and Vinayaka. One should fully worship Mahalakshmi with the hymns that begin, Salutation to the Goddess.
In the worship of the three descents, the hymn-mantras then have their support. And this eighteen-armed one, crusher of the buffalo, is to be worshipped.
Mahalakshmi is Mahakali, and she herself is called Sarasvati. She is the sovereign of merits and sins, the great sovereign of all the worlds.
The one by whom the ender of Mahisha is worshipped becomes lord of the world. One should worship Chandika, supporter of the worlds, tender toward devotees,
with the guest-offering and the rest, with ornaments, with excellent scents and flowers, with incenses, lamps, and food-offerings joined with foods of many kinds,
with a bali marked by blood, with meat, and with wine, O king, with the water of sipping after the bow, and with fragrant sandal,
and with betel joined with camphor, accompanied by a feeling of devotion. In front, on the left side of the Goddess, one should worship the great asura whose head was cut off,
the buffalo, by whom union with the sovereign was obtained. On the right, in front, one should worship the lion entire, the lord who is dharma,
the mount of the Goddess, by whom what moves and what does not move is held. Then, with joined hands, one should praise her with these deeds,
with one, or with the middle one, and not with one of the other two here. One should not recite half a deed. One who recites so obtains a gap.
One should praise this Mother of the world with the hymn-mantras, or otherwise. Having made circumambulation and bows, with joined hands at the head,
one should ask forgiveness of the supporter of the world, again and again, undistracted. And at each verse one should offer milk-rice with sesame and clarified butter.
Or one should offer an auspicious oblation to Chandika with the hymn-mantras. Collected, one should worship the Goddess with the words of salutation upon salutation.
Restrained, with joined hands, bowed, and having placed the breaths in oneself, one should meditate on the Goddess Chandika for a long time, and become made of her.
Whoever worships the supreme sovereign in this way, with devotion, every day, having enjoyed enjoyments as desired, would obtain union with the Goddess.
Whoever does not worship Chandika, tender toward devotees, every day, the supreme sovereign, having made his merits into ashes, would burn them.

Therefore worship, O king, the great sovereign of all the worlds. By the manner that has been stated, you will obtain happiness through Chandika. Thus the secret of the modifications, in the Devi Mahatmya of the Surya-Savarnika manvantara in the Markandeya Purana, is complete.
